original_question: Let n >= 3 and consider the elliptic eigenvalue problem div(A grad u) - q u + lambda rho u = 0 in Omega with u = 0 on ∂Omega, where A is uniformly elliptic and only Hölder continuous rather than Lipschitz, q and rho belong to L^infinity(Omega), and rho >= K^(-1) > 0. Under what conditions on A that do not imply unique continuation for the associated equation div(A grad u) - q u + lambda rho u = 0 does Courant's nodal domain theorem still remain valid?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the open problem in the section titled “Extending Courant’s nodal domain theorem,” labeled “Problem 7.1 (Courant)” in the PDF version and appearing as the same statement under “Problem 6.1” in the arXiv HTML rendering: determine conditions on the coefficient matrix A, weaker than hypotheses guaranteeing unique continuation, that still ensure the full Courant nodal domain theorem for the variable-coefficient Dirichlet eigenvalue problem. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the operator div(A∇u)−qu+λρu=0 with Dirichlet boundary data, the restriction n≥3, the standing assumptions q,ρ∈L∞(Ω) with ρ bounded below by a positive constant, the contrast between Lipschitz and Hölder regularity of A, and the central issue of preserving Courant’s nodal domain theorem under hypotheses on A that do not force unique continuation. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
missing_details: The paper assumes Ω is a bounded, connected open subset of ℝ^n. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

A=A(x) is taken to be a symmetric matrix-valued coefficient field; this is part of the standing notation imported from the earlier elliptic discussion. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
The exact ellipticity hypothesis is K^{-1}|ξ|^2 ≤ A(x)ξ·ξ ≤ K|ξ|^2 for all x,ξ∈ℝ^n. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

The official problem is about the full spectral statement of Courant’s theorem: every eigenfunction u_m corresponding to the m-th Dirichlet eigenvalue λ_m should have at most m nodal domains. Your draft refers to the theorem but does not unpack this conclusion. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

The paper’s open problem is slightly broader than your wording: it asks for conditions on A not implying unique continuation, without restricting a priori to the Hölder class. Hölder continuity is only the motivating nearby case where the full theorem is not known. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
If one mentions the Hölder regime explicitly, the paper states it as |A(x)−A(y)| ≤ E|x−y|^α for some α∈(0,1) and E>0. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

The nearby context also records the sharp known benchmarks: Courant’s nodal domain theorem is known when n=2 or A is Lipschitz, because then unique continuation holds for the associated equation; for n≥3 with Hölder A, only the weaker bound that u_m has at most 2(m−1) nodal domains for every m≥2 is stated. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))

The paper treats q and ρ as fixed background coefficients satisfying q,ρ∈L∞(Ω) and ρ≥K^{-1}>0; the open question asks only for additional conditions on A. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
refined_question: Let Ω⊂ℝ^n be a bounded, connected open set with n≥3, and consider the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem div(A(x)∇u)−q(x)u+λρ(x)u=0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, where A=A(x) is a symmetric matrix field satisfying K^{-1}|ξ|^2≤A(x)ξ·ξ≤K|ξ|^2 for all x,ξ∈ℝ^n, and q,ρ∈L∞(Ω) with ρ≥K^{-1}>0. Under what additional conditions on A, which do not imply the unique continuation property for the associated equation div(A∇u)−q(x)u+λρ(x)u=0, does the full Courant nodal domain theorem still hold; that is, for every m, must each eigenfunction u_m associated with the m-th eigenvalue λ_m have at most m nodal domains? ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because the paper itself isolates exactly this open problem in the section on extending Courant’s theorem to variable-coefficient elliptic operators. The surrounding sentences supply the standing hypotheses on Ω, A, q, and ρ, explain the known positive cases (n=2 or A Lipschitz), and identify the Hölder-continuous regime as the motivating non-UCP setting where only a weaker 2(m−1) nodal-domain bound is known. Your draft is therefore close, but it needs the spectral/nodal conclusion spelled out explicitly and should not narrow the official question to the Hölder class unless that narrowing is announced as context rather than as part of the statement. ([rendiconti.dmi.units.it](https://rendiconti.dmi.units.it/volumi/52/031.pdf))
